styles.name: Black denim retail bib apron, full width pocket divided into four, double pen pocket, zip pocket, eyelets and D ring loops for the detachable cross-over straps — Hickory's 5 star logo in gold
styles.desc: RETAIL BIB APRON · Full width pocket divided into four · Double pen pocket left breast as worn with two stitch lines forming three pen pockets · Zip pocket set to the left front as worn · Eyelets at the waist and lower studs at the top of the bib for the detachable neck / waist tie (the strap OHSTRAP03DEN is cut separately with its own routing card) · D ring loops at each side set into the top of the pocket hem stitching · Contrast gold topstitching · Hanger loop at the lower edge of the bib facing · Black OH logo'd towel loop · Hickory's 5 star logo in gold above the wide pocket, right side as worn
fabrics: Black denim 100% cotton Art Murray 315 gsm (P and R fabrics) — rating 0.75 m on the sheet; All Costings carries 0.85 m and the lay plan's marker 0627001 is 2.62 m for 4 (0.655 m)
trims: THREAD — COATS EPIC 80'S GOLD 02362 for all stitching on the denim — cost per metre (Sage holds the shade as the 40's gold)
Set into the right side seam as worn, 4 cm down from the top edge.
Oliver Harvey wash instructions under the woven label: 100% cotton · 50° wash · no bleach · 2 dot iron · no tumble dry · dry clean.
Oliver Harvey red tab set to the pen pocket: top left hand corner of the pocket, level with the top of the pocket.
Black Oliver Harvey logo'd tape, cut 39 cm, Oliver Harvey to read from top to bottom. Sage holds the black OH tape as the non tangle tie CMP-OH-NTT-25-03, costed per metre: 0.39 m per apron.
Lower studs set to the top of the bib, use the marker: 4 per apron. The female part is on the detachable strap OHSTRAP03DEN.

18 cm (7") black zip with antique brass metal teeth, single closed end, MGKBC56C/7/18 col 580, 1 per apron. No Sage code for the metal zip (Sage holds spiral zips only); the trims master prices it at £0.39.
Set with a self fabric loop and inserted into the top of the pocket hem topstitching, 1 at each side: 2 per apron.

010B/7P - 011B antique brass invert nipple rivet and post. Set one at the top of each of the three stitch lines of the wide pocket and one to each outside edge of the pen pocket: 5 per apron. No Sage code on the trims list (the trims master prices the rivet 011B/AB at £0.00962 and the prong 010B/7P at £0.01693).
30E/R AB 30 mm eyelet. Set so the centre of the eyelet is 3 cm from the finished top edge and 3 cm in from the finished side seam: 2 per apron.
The ring for each 30 mm eyelet: 2 per apron.
Black knitted tape for the hanger loop, set to the base of the bib facing, cut at 8 cm: 0.08 m per apron.
mfg: Embroidery: Hickory's 5 star logo (20 cm) in gold thread, set above the wide pocket, right side as worn. Centre of the embroidery in line with the twin needle pocket divide and level with the zip pocket.

Cut the hanger tape at 8 cm. Set centrally to the bib facing into the lower edge. Tack in position taking a 1.5 cm seam of tape at each end: the hanger loop measures 5 cm from end to end (see the diagram on the sheet).

Stitch down the bib facing to form the 5.5 cm topstitching of the front bib. Ensure this topstitching is an even width from the top of the bib and equal at each side: if it is unlevel it will show when the straps are set.
6 mm topstitch the top of the bib.

Set the towel loop: cut at 39 cm and fold in half. Set to the armhole curve 10 cm from the side seam cut edge, left side as worn, Oliver Harvey to read down. Stitch down the towel loop to follow the armhole stitching.

Make the zip pocket. Set the pocket bag to the apron with the right sides of the fabrics together; steck holes to be in line with the notch in the side seam, use the marker for the position. Stitch the box opening for the zip: use the steck holes for the centre of the box and stitch 1 cm past the steck hole, a 3 stitch wide (1 cm) box. The opening is 3 cm down from the cut edge and central within the width of the pocket bag.

Cut the opening for the zip. Press the opening before topstitching the zip, or edgestitch the inside long edges to help the seams roll. Set the zip (when closed the puller is to the left side seam as worn). Edgestitch all round. Set a second row of twin needle stitching to the sides and bottom of the pocket. Close the pocket bags: the lower bag extends 2 cm past the top bag to neaten the top edge as notched; edges enclosed on the inside. Double turn the top edge of the pocket. Twin needle stitch the top of the zip opening, stitching through the pocket bag when topstitching the top of the pocket.
Set the pocket hem: double turn 1 cm and twin needle stitch. To reduce bulk at the ends start the double turn 1.5 cm from each end (nick into the turning to let it lie flat).
Set the wide pocket: with right sides together set the cut edge to the notch and stitch a 1 cm seam. Pull the pocket up onto the apron and tack the sides in position.
Make the D ring loops: fold over each side to the notches, finished width to fit the D ring. Edgestitch both long edges.
Double turn the armholes and topstitch 6 mm.
Double turn the side seams and hem and topstitch 12 mm. Set the labels in the right side seam as worn, 4 cm down from the finished top edge.

Insert one end of the D ring loop into the pocket hem and stitch down the pocket hem to the width of the D ring. Fold the D ring loop over and insert the other end. Topstitch down following the bottom row of twin needle stitching.

Twin needle pocket stitch lines: from the left side as worn set the first row of twin needle stitching 18.5 cm from the finished side seam, the second stitch line with a 6 cm gap. From the right side as worn set the pocket stitch line 18.5 cm from the finished side seam to the first row of twin needle stitching.
Set the pen pocket hem: turn 1 + 2.2 cm and twin needle stitch, the bottom row of stitching 2 cm from the top of the pocket. Stitch in the contrast thread.

Set the pen pocket to the left side of the bib as worn: top edge 8 cm down from the top of the finished bib and 3.5 cm in from the finished armhole. Twin needle three sides. Set the Oliver Harvey tax tab level with the top of the pocket, left side of the pocket as worn.
Set a single stitch line down at 2.5 cm from each side of the pen pocket (two single stitch lines to form three pen pockets).
fin: Set the rivets: one at each side of the top of the pen pocket and one at the top of each stitch line on the wide pocket.
Set the eyelets: centre of the eyelet 3 cm in from the side seam and 3 cm down from the top.

Check and ensure the bib's 5.5 cm topstitching is equal at both sides of the bib. Set the lower studs to the bib, use the marker: centre of the top stud 1.8 cm from the side of the bib and 1.4 cm down from the top edge, second stud 3 cm spacing vertically down.
Bartack the end of each D ring loop to re-inforce the pocket opening: 2 bartacks.
Trim, press, fold and wrap in Oliver Harvey tissue. Set the product sticker to the tissue and set into a bag.
styles.tol: Tolerance ± 1 cm (length from bib to hem ± 1.5 cm)
styles.brandPlace: Hickory's 5 star logo (20 cm) in gold thread, set above the wide pocket, right side as worn: centre of the embroidery in line with the twin needle pocket divide and level with the zip pocket.
styles.note: Works order OHHICAPP062703DEN/DS for Hickory's, Oliver Harvey, issued by Gail (JH created 23/1/17 based on SR533; code amended re CW JH 2/5/19). The bib version of the Hickory's waist apron OHHICAPP062803DEN: OHAP0534 variant 0627 with the wide pocket, pen pocket, zip pocket and D ring loops. The detachable cross-over neck / waist straps are the black denim OHSTRAP03DEN, cut separately on their own routing card. Rating 0.75 m on the sheet; All Costings carries 0.85 m and the lay plan's marker 0627001 is 2.62 m for 4 (0.655 m). The sheet lists the rivets as 5 in all (three on the wide pocket stitch lines, one each side of the pen pocket) where its finishing line says 3. The logo artwork is not on the sheet; its sketch of the apron is on the record and, with the hanger loop diagram, in works-orders/OHHICAPP062703DEN-DS-Hickorys.xlsx.
